# solo-msa_v2-gemini-3-8-flash-core-stepcounter

<!-- Generated by tools/export_results.py. Edit only the Experiment and Observations sections. -->

## Experiment

One agent implements both features on the `core` subset (10 pairs chosen to represent the full benchmark, including three pairs where both features change the same function: `dspy_task/8563`, `go_chi_task/27`, and `react_hook_form_task/153`). Setup: `gemini-3.8-flash` at `high` thinking, 100 steps, compaction at 28K, and the per-turn step counter. It is the `solo` reference for `coop --git` on the same pairs, to look for coordination failures that `flash_10` rarely shows.

## Observations

- 5/10. `core` is harder than `flash_10` for this setup (7/10 there): all 10 agents used every one of their 100 steps, though 8 of 10 pushed work along the way.
- Of the three same-function pairs, `dspy_task/8563` and `go_chi_task/27` passed only one feature each, and `react_hook_form_task/153` pushed nothing. `pallets_jinja_task/1621` (features 6 and 10) also pushed nothing.
- Agents compacted their context about 12 times each, so these pairs need more steps or more context than this budget gives.
- 13 calls were retried because of the API rate limit, which only slows `solo` agents down.
